prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Thrips in my plant room😬.

Any suggestions on eradicating them. Yesterday, I began spraying with a solution (70% alcohol / 29% water / 1% peppermint oil). I plan to spray all leaves every week. I have read that this will help control Thrips but not eradicate them. Any advice from people that have overcome thrips?

I have over 80 plants in my plant room and need to aggressively kill this invader. Some of my orchids are over 25 yrs old.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
This looks like **thrips feeding damage**. The fine yellow-white speckling across the leaf surface is typical of thrips rasping at the cells and sucking out the contents. Look closely at the undersides and the new growth for slivers of insects or small black specks (their droppings) to confirm.

1. **Confirm and monitor.** Tap a few affected stems over a sheet of white paper and look for tiny, fast-moving slivers. Hang a few blue sticky traps (about $10 for a pack of 10) among the plants to track whether the population is falling.

2. **Spray more often.** Your alcohol and peppermint spray kills thrips on contact but not eggs, which hatch in about a week. Spray every 3 to 4 days for about 3 weeks, covering the undersides of leaves, soil surface and pot rims. Test one leaf on each plant type first and wait 24 hours, since alcohol can scorch some plants, especially soft or waxy-leaved ones.

3. **Alternate with spinosad for stubborn plants.** For heavily infested plants, use a spinosad spray (such as Monterey Garden Insect Spray, about $12) according to the label, on days you are not using the alcohol mix. This targets the larvae that survive contact sprays.

4. **Isolate the worst plants.** Move heavily infested plants away from the rest of the collection until they are clear, to slow spread between plants.

Thrips are persistent, so expect several weeks of treatment before you see new growth free of damage.
